name: Harkonen
label: Hydra Head
lede: Harkonen started in Tacoma in 1997 as a five-piece hardcore band, lost members until three were left, cut two records for Hydra Head and played its last show at Bumbershoot in 2005.

eras.title: Five guys, then three
eras.text: Harkonen started as a noisy five-piece in the line of Deadguy and Kiss It Goodbye. Singers and guitarists came and went on two 7" singles, and by the end of 1999 Ben Verellen, Casey Hardy and Matt Howard were what was left.

years.h: Two founders are gone after the first 7"
years.p: The self-titled 7" came out on Unjust in 1997. Vocalist Mike Jones and guitarist Chris Vancourt left soon after, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Label bio text puts the band at this point in the line of Deadguy and Kiss It Goodbye. The name comes from the Harkonnen family in Frank Herbert's Dune.

years.h: Aaron "Edge" Connell takes the mic for Hung to Dry
years.p: The Hung to Dry 7" came out on Excursion with Connell on vocals. He later founded [[Himsa|198bed0f-a246-4116-9c7a-0140cbd372b7]].
years.xp: Wikipedia says Connell came over from Grip and left around 1999 along with guitarist Neihl Brady. Last.fm says he left to focus on other projects, Himsa among them. Wikipedia's Himsa page lists him in that band from 1998 to 1999.

years.h: A CD on Wreck-Age, and three players left
years.p: The first full-length came out on Wreck-Age. By then the band was Ben Verellen, Casey Hardy and Matt Howard.
years.xp: Sources disagree on who played what and when guitarist Bill Quinby left. Wikipedia has him gone around 1999, with Verellen, Hardy and Howard holding through 2005. Another bio has Verellen and Howard sharing vocals, with Hardy replacing Quinby.

eras.title: Hydra Head takes them in
eras.text: As a trio Harkonen drifted from Deadguy-style hardcore toward noise rock, with Scratch Acid and Nirvana in the mix, and landed on Aaron Turner's label. Two Hydra Head records are what most people know them for.

years.h: Charge! comes out on tiny Ataque Sonoro
years.p: The CD followed the self-titled album, a year before the move to Hydra Head.
Five songs, including "Kildow's Song" and "Hey You Millionaires, Get Out of That Garbage." It came as a CD EP and a 7" on [[Aaron Turner|db3ca919-a4ab-451a-8f03-e51310cfd866]]'s label.
years.xp: Harkonen then toured nationally with Hydra Head bands including Isis, according to Last.fm's bio.

years.src: Wikipedia: Shake Harder Boy · Wikipedia: Harkonen · YouTube: Harkonen, Smile Pretty
years.h: Eleven songs in about 27 minutes with Matt Bayles
years.p: Shake Harder Boy was recorded at Studio Litho and Avast! Recording Co. It includes "Smile Pretty," "Baristas Get Stalked" and the 5:29 closer "Settle Here."
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits the production to [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]] and the band. A reviewer at vaguely-offensive gave it five out of five and set it beside [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]] and Pelican for pummeling heft that still left room for experiments.

Harkonen kept playing it live for years. The 2012 Neumos footage of "Smile Pretty" is one of the reunion clips.

years.big: "We loved recording and playing together, and nobody bought the records."
q: loved that band, and we loved those songs, and we loved recording and playing together - and nobody bought the records.
years.h: Ben Verellen starts Roy with Dave Verellen of [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]]
years.p: Roy was a Tacoma band with Dave Verellen, Brian Cook (both ex-Botch) and Ben Verellen.
years.xp: Roy put out its EPs from 2002, then Big City Sin and Small Town Redemption in 2004 on Fueled by Ramen, made with Matt Bayles. Killed John Train followed in 2006. Dave Verellen's line is as Wikipedia prints it from the 2009 Revolver interview.

years.h: Dancing on Initial is the last EP under their own name
years.p: Out on Initial Records. One reviewer called it looser than Shake Harder Boy.
years.xp: Last.fm says the band began to lose steam around the recording of Dancing.

eras.title: Two splits and a festival stage
eras.text: The last two years went to split releases, with Verellen also playing in other bands. Harkonen ended on the bill at a Seattle festival.

years.p: Released on Happy Couples Never Last, per Wikipedia's discography.

yt: Payday Loans, split with These Arms Are Snakes
years.h: Harkonen and These Arms Are Snakes split Like a Virgin
years.p: The last release was a split EP with the Seattle band These Arms Are Snakes. Ben Verellen also played additional bass on their debut and drummed for them on tour in 2005.
years.xp: YouTube lists the split as 2004 and Wikipedia as 2005, so the date is uncertain. Wikipedia's Ben Verellen article says he was These Arms Are Snakes' touring drummer in 2005.

years.big: "Stormed the northwest music scene for nearly eight years."
q: stormed the northwest music scene for nearly eight years
years.h: Harkonen plays its last show at Bumbershoot
years.p: The band ended in 2005 with a final performance at Seattle's Bumbershoot festival.
years.xp: Last.fm says Harkonen had begun to lose momentum around its final EP. Ben Verellen went on to Roy, Helms Alee and These Arms Are Snakes' drum stool.

eras.title: A reunion, Helms Alee and a Botch cover
eras.text: Harkonen played reunion shows in 2011 and 2012 but made no new records. Ben Verellen kept busy with Helms Alee and his amp shop, and showed up on a Botch cover in 2022.

years.cap: Helms Alee at Great American Music Hall, San Francisco
years.src: Wikipedia: Ben Verellen · Wikipedia: Harkonen · YouTube: Harkonen, Catching Cold · YouTube: Harkonen, Easy Prey
yt: Catching Cold, The Shakedown, Bellingham, March 18, 2011
years.h: Helms Alee starts, and Harkonen plays again later
years.p: Verellen's next long-running band has put out seven albums since 2008, per Wikipedia. He also builds guitar amps as Verellen Amplifiers.
years.xp: Harkonen did not stay buried. Fan video shows reunion sets at The Shakedown in Bellingham on March 18, 2011 and The Top of Tacoma on March 20, 2011, then Neumos in Seattle on June 30, 2012. Wikipedia says the band toured in 2012 with The Atlas Moth and Whores.

years.h: Verellen sings on a Botch cover with Kurt Ballou
years.p: Ballou, Dimitri Minakakis and Rorschach's Andrew Gormley joined him for Botch's "To Our Friends in the Great White North," published June 7, 2022 as the first Hardcore Summer clip from Two Minutes to Late Night.
years.xp: Louder notes that Verellen sang backing vocals at Botch's last show. [[Matt Bayles|e294077f-71eb-401f-a36a-f2dbcbd75863]], who mixed the original We Are the Romans, mixed the cover too.
